is_anopheles.evidence: Field trials identified collected mosquitoes including Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles coustani (page 5, 'persisting into the trial period... assigned them to one of six genus/species level classifications (Anopheles gambiae s.s., Anopheles coustani, Culex spp., Mansonia spp., Aedes aegypti and Aedes simpsoni)').

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study evaluates the repellent efficacy of catnip essential oil and does not perform any molecular genotyping of insecticide-resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No insecticide-resistance marker genotype or allele data are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were field-collected via human landing catch in Eastern Uganda (Mugiti and Kamonkoli subcounties of Budaka District) (page 3, 'Human landing catch field trial design and procedure').

is_primary_study.evidence: The study presents primary field trial research on repellent lotions.

sub_country_location.evidence: Trials were conducted at Mugiti and Kamonkoli subcounties, Budaka District, Eastern Uganda (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections took place in June 2024 and May-June 2025 (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field evaluation of a catnip essential oil repellent lotion.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary data contains landing count spreadsheets and GC-MS spectral traces; no resistance genotyping was conducted in this study.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the mosquito repellent efficacy of a topical lotion containing catnip essential oil compared to DEET using human landing catches in Budaka District, Uganda. It does not perform any insecticide resistance marker genotyping or bioassays.
